newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda profits rocket on weak yen, RV sales.
newsitem.headline: Honda profits rocket on weak yen, RV sales.

text.p: Honda Motor said on Friday that its third-quarter profits jumped more than threefold from a year ago, boosted by strong recreational-vehicle sales and a weak yen. It added that it expects record profits for the year.
"The profits were bigger than we expected," a Honda spokesman said.
The company said its group net profit in the October-December period was a record 61.92 billion yen ($503 million), up a staggering 237.3 percent from the year earlier.
Its profits for the nine-months to December 31 were also a record, at 156.82 billion yen ($1.27 billion).
Honda raised its group earnings forecast for the full year to March 31 to a record 220 billion yen ($1.78 billion) from its previous forecast of 200 billion yen ($1.62 billion).
Group net profit is the combined profit after tax and costs of Honda and its Japanese and overseas units.
The yen 's recent weakness gave Honda's profits a boost by making its foreign currency-denominated overseas revenue worth more in terms of yen, the company said.
"A decline of 1 yen against the dollar translates to about 6 to 7 billion yen at Honda this business year," said Nobuaki Yanachi, a senior analyst at Kankaku Research.
The Honda spokesman said the company expected the average yen rate for fiscal 1996/97 to be 110 against 91 a year earlier.
The dollar stood at around 123 yen in Tokyo on Friday.
The Honda spokesman said the weak yen saved the company 90 billion yen ($731 million) while cost-cutting measures saved another 52 billion yen ($422 million).
Honda said robust sales of its recreational vehicles, which now account for about half its car sales in Japan, also gave its earnings an edge.
The company said its domestic vehicle sales were likely to reach around 770,000 units in fiscal 1996/97, up from its November forecast of 760,000 units.
It actual sales in fiscal 1995/96 were 654,000 units.
-- Mitsuo Suzuki, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8017 ($=123 yen)
